newsitem.title: USA: Continental chairman says talks on track.
newsitem.headline: Continental chairman says talks on track.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc chairman Gordon Bethune said on Friday contract talks with the carrier's pilots were going well and that he expected to have a new pact by July 1.

Bethune, speaking to reporters after the company's annual shareholders' meeting, said Continental and the pilots had asked to bring in a federal mediator "to keep things moving" as negotiators reached the most critical issue - salaries.
"We're down to the money now...everything else is mostly resolved," he said.

Bethune said bringing in a mediator did not signal problems in the talks, which began April 2. Rather, Continental management generally favors using a mediator to keep negotiations from bogging down, he said.
"We used a mediator from the outset in our (successful) negotiations with flight attendants (last year)," he said.
The company has said it would like to have a new pact with pilots, who are seeking a pay increase of up to 38 percent, by July 1 when the current contract expires.
"Oh absolutely, I don't see why not," Bethune said when asked if he thought that date could be met.
Bethune also said Continental, which had merger talks with Delta Air Lines Inc last year, was not now seeking a partner. "We don't have any plans to talk to anybody," he said.
Bethune said industry conditions had changed so that massive consolidation of airlines appeared less likely than before, making it less critical for Continental to merge.

He said the company was now focused on attracting more business flyers and paring its debt and interest costs. As part of the effort to cut costs, Bethune said Continental had asked Boeing Co to "give us a proposal" about becoming the airline's sole supplier of planes.

Bethune also said Continental was still in talks to buy a stake in Aerolineas Argentinas, but he could not say when the deal might be done or how much it might cost. He said Continental was seeking a big say in management, but not voting control of the airline.
American Airlines is also negotiating to buy a piece of the Argentinian carrier.
